description:
About the Fellowship

The UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi) is funded by the Government of Japan. It provides 10 fellowships in 2026 with grants up to US$10,000 for 3-9 months of research at Japanese universities or research institutions. This master's / PhD / postdoctoral opening at UNESCO centres on Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships 2026 Japan. Research areas covered include Artificial Intelligence, Environmental Science. The host institution is in Paris, France. According to the listing, full funding is provided; financial support is listed as Up to US$10,000 (lump sum).. Interested candidates should note the deadline: 30 September 2026.

Financial Coverage

  • Grant up to US$10,000 (lump sum).
  • Covers international and domestic travel, accommodation, medical insurance (mandatory, deducted from amount), personal subsistence, and research-related expenses.
  • Does NOT cover tuition fees, equipment or computers, publication costs, or conference participation.

Eligibility and Requirements

  • National of an invited Member State.
  • Age 40 or under at time of application.
  • Minimum Master's degree in a relevant field with strong research potential.
  • Proficiency in language of host institution.
  • Must obtain acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or institution.

Important: Eligible Countries

Only invited Member States for 2026 cycle: Africa (47 countries), Bahrain, Asia-Pacific (Maldives, Timor-Leste, Fiji, Singapore, PNG, Samoa, and others), Latin America and Caribbean, Turkiye, and Ukraine.

Note: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, and Nepal are NOT on the list. Confirm with your country's National Commission before applying.

Research Areas (2026 Cycle)

  1. Heritage Conservation and Management.
  2. AI for Sustainable Management of Natural Resources and Climate Action.
  3. Ethical, Inclusive and Human-Centred AI for Sustainable Development.
  4. AI for Sustainable Cities, Infrastructure and Societal Resilience.
  5. AI and Education.

Application dates

MilestoneDate
Application deadline30 September 2026, midnight Paris time
Research periodFebruary 2027 to December 2027

Application Process

  1. Download Application Guide and Annexes 1-5 from UNESCO website.
  2. Prepare application form, research proposal, and language certificate.
  3. Submit through your country's National Commission for UNESCO. Do not submit directly to UNESCO.
  4. Internal deadlines may be earlier (some countries close in late August).

Official Link

https://www.unesco.org/en/fellowships/keizo-obuchi

Important Notes

  • This is a capped grant, not a fully funded scholarship.
  • Japanese supervisor acceptance must be arranged by the applicant.
  • Program has funded 291 researchers from 101 countries since 2001.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 30 September 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.

Open the official application page ↗
